name: qa_modules
title: OS-FINALQA, Modules (OS-TAPCALC, OS-H1, OS-H2a and OS-H2b, new Community OS behaviour): the Tap Calc, MIDI Monitor, Loudness VU, Scope Spectrum and Tuner apps from /modules/apps of a test card: the first-launch question (QA-MOD-009 needs a fresh `reset` before the run: the confirm is remembered per boot), tap tempo, the 2 s reset, manual BPM, the Hz page, Delete, setting the project's tempo with F2 and undoing it; the MIDI Monitor against messages sent from the PC with amidi. The tempo is read from the shots (the app's text is not in the state line). Nothing is written to the card

steps.say: OS-TAPCALC rows QA-MOD-002..008, OS-H1 rows QA-MOD-009..016 of docs/qa/catalogue/modules.md (ADR 0014 slice H1, new Community OS behaviour). Precondition: a TEST card with tapcalc.tmod and midimon.tmod in /modules/apps (the packed files of o3m_tapcalc_tmod and o3m_midimon_tmod: build-os-*/modules/*.tmod), the project loaded (its tempo is what PROJECT shows). The cursor walks to each app by its name (`sel=` of `diag state`, OS-SMALLFIX6), so other apps on the card do not matter. The pads are tapped by the runner over the console, so its timing jitters by tens of ms: the BPM reads within a few percent of the requested one. MIDI in comes from the PC: `amidi -p hw:1,0,0 -S "90 3C 64"` (USB; hw:1,0,0 is the Tracker's USB MIDI port on that PC: `amidi -l` says). The F7 + F8 exit chord steps are sent as a burst (one back-to-back run of console commands, inside the firmware's 40 ms chord window). QA-MOD-009 is boot-state dependent: Tap Calc asks its first-launch confirm once per boot, so run `o3console reset` (and wait for the unit) just before this scenario; a second run on the same boot starts Tap Calc at the first F1 and the question steps fail. Nothing is written to the card

steps.say: QA-MOD-008, by hand (Tap Calc holds edit_project: its first F1 per boot only asks, a second F1 starts it, QA-MOD-009): leave the app (F7 + F8 follows), open the Pattern screen (Pattern key) and read the tempo in the info/status line: it is the one the app set. Press F8 (UNDO) once: the old tempo is back. Then come back to MODULES. Also try to set a tempo below 40.0 BPM (Shift is not needed: encoder down to 20.0, F2): the page must say `NOT SET: THE PROJECT TAKES 40 - 800 BPM` and the project keeps its tempo. Record both in the report

steps.say: OS-H2a rows QA-MOD-017..023 of docs/qa/catalogue/modules.md (ADR 0014 slice H2a, ABI 1.4, new Community OS behaviour: the audio tap and the Loudness VU app). Precondition: loudness.tmod too in /modules/apps of the test card (the packed file of o3m_loudness_tmod: build-os-*/modules/loudness.tmod), and a project loaded that plays several tracks (a song). The runner uses PLAY on the app page; if the transport does not start from there, start the song from the Song screen first and come back to MODULES with the Navigator. QA-MOD-019 needs a signal on the line input (a tone from the PC into the Tracker's line in, or any music), QA-MOD-020 needs it loud enough to reach full scale. Nothing is written to the card

steps.note: the tap's cost counters (and the cpu ones) start from zero for QA-MOD-023
the cursor from MIDI Monitor up to Loudness VU, until sel=loudness
QA-MOD-017: Loudness VU starts with no question (it only listens)

QA-MOD-017: LOUDNESS VU, SOURCE MASTER, PEAK and RMS empty with -INF, the 0 / -6 / -12 ... scale, HOLD -INF MAX -INF, a dark clip lamp, CLIPS 0, an empty RMS HISTORY frame, two hint lines; SOURCE (2) and HOLD (3) on the left
QA-MOD-018: start the song with the app page up
(if the transport did not start from here, start the song from the Song screen and reopen the app)

QA-MOD-018: PEAK and RMS bars moving with the song, readouts in dBFS (a normal mix reads roughly -30 to -3), the white hold marker on PEAK, HOLD and MAX filled, the history line drawing from the right edge

expect: tap: master, \d+ blocks, write cycles last \d+ mean \d+ max \d+ \(max [\d.]+ us\)
steps.note: QA-MOD-023 (Loudness VU: LEVELS ONLY, the render stores no samples since OS-BUG-TAPWRITE): the tap work of a block as the render timed it. SOFT (reported, not failing) until the next image gives figures: the max is a wall-clock max and this run plays the song, so an interrupt inside the window shows as max. A max of 3600 cycles (20 us) or more is reported as a soft failure (ADR 0014). The mean is judged against `diag bench kernels` k_mono_mix + k_meter + about 150, not against 360. Note the three figures in the report; image int.6 (samples stored) read mean 1765, max 6077

Then press Delete: CLIPS 0, HOLD / MAX -INF, the history empties

steps.say: OS-H2b rows QA-MOD-024..033 of docs/qa/catalogue/modules.md (ADR 0014 slice H2b, ABI 1.4, new Community OS behaviour: the Tuner and the Scope Spectrum apps, both on the audio tap). Precondition: scope.tmod and tuner.tmod (the packed files of o3m_scope_tmod and o3m_tuner_tmod: build-os-*/modules/scope.tmod and tuner.tmod) copied into /modules/apps of the test card AFTER the earlier part of this scenario. Then F2 RESCAN on MODULES below. The apps are reached by name: the cursor goes to the top of the list and Down until `sel=` of `diag state` names the app (OS-SMALLFIX6). MIDI comes from the PC: `amidi -p hw:1,0,0 -S "90 45 64"` plays MIDI note 69 (440 Hz on an instrument tuned to concert pitch, A4 for the tuner) on the current instrument and `-S "80 45 00"` stops it: select the Sine or the Chip module on the current instrument first, so that the pitch is exact (a sample plays its own pitch). The tuner and the scope read the MASTER output (SOURCE 2) for these steps. QA-MOD-027 and QA-MOD-032 need a tone from the PC into the Tracker's line input. Nothing is written to the card

Silence or noise reads `FREE RUN`

QA-MOD-024: TUNER, `A4 440 HZ   INPUT` at the top right, NO SIGNAL in place of the note, the needle scale -50 ... +50 with no needle, `FREQ --`, `CENTS --`, CONFIDENCE 0 %, two hint lines; A4 (440) and SOURCE (1) on the left

Within about a second the note name `A4` shows large, `FREQ 440.0 HZ` (within a few tenths), `CENTS` within a few of 0 and the needle at the middle in the in-tune colour; the name and the needle stay put while the note is held (no flipping, the cents move by a cent or two at most)

The range is 415 to 466 (the encoder stops there). Put it back to 440

steps.note: QA-MOD-026: A4 432 at the top right, CENTS +32, the needle right of centre in orange

steps.say: QA-MOD-027: stop the note: `amidi -p hw:1,0,0 -S "80 45 00"`. After about a second the note is replaced by NO SIGNAL, FREQ -- and CENTS --, the needle disappears. Then SOURCE 1 (INPUT) with a tone from the PC into the line input: the tuner reads it (440 Hz from the PC reads A4); with white noise or music with no clear pitch, or with nothing connected, it stays at NO SIGNAL (it never invents a note from noise)

steps.note: QA-MOD-027: NO SIGNAL, FREQ --, CENTS --, no needle
the exit chord F7 + F8: back to MODULES, the render stops writing the tap

QA-MOD-033: the tap is off again after the app stopped, and the render did not underrun while the apps ran. Open each of the two apps for 30 s with a held note and check that MODULES lists neither as quarantined (a view_draw over its 4 ms is blanked and the app is quarantined for the boot): the per-frame microseconds of the two apps are not shown by any console command yet, so their figure on the unit is still owed

steps.say: OS-MODPITCH rows QA-MOD-099..106 of docs/qa/catalogue/modules.md (ABI 1.8, new Community OS behaviour; needs the MOD-ABI image). By ear, a note held on a track, on TB-303, then Chip, then FM. Nothing here is scripted: play the pattern and compare with the same pattern on a sampler instrument.

QA-MOD-100: a note held for several steps; a step with Slide up 16 and no note, later Slide down 32 and no note. Expected: one semitone up after one step, then it stays; the next goes to two semitones below the note; no new envelope, no click.

QA-MOD-101: Glide 10 on a note a fifth above the previous. Expected: a legato slide over 200 ms, ONE envelope (no restart); after a gap the new note starts normally and still glides; the first note of the track is plain. On FM an octave Glide: listen for zipper (the pitch is a staircase of one block).
QA-MOD-102: Slide and Glide on one track; the same note again; a plain note. Expected: Slide wins; the repeated note is a tie; the plain note retriggers at its own pitch.
QA-MOD-103: Chord 4 in one column and Arp 7 in the other on TB-303: the tones play one after another, retriggered. Arp alone: one note. Chord alone: the root.
QA-MOD-104: with an old card copy of a module of ABI 1.7 or below (if one is on the card), the same pattern has no slide and no legato.

QA-MOD-105 / 106: open the Instrument page of TB-303, Chip and FM: the key row says SOUND/MODS, TONE/ENV/PITCH/OSC/FX, OP1..OP4; Chip Wave and Duty and FM Algorithm show names. Check the page names are legible on the key tile. QA-MOD-107: on TB-303 (two pages) F1 and F2 carry names and F3, F4, F5 are blank (no dimmed 17-24 / 25-32); a blank key does nothing. Then a module with no parameters: F1..F5 are all blank, F1 does nothing, and the info line reads MODULE <name> NO PARAMETERS: nothing to edit.

steps.note: MOD-ABI cost: start the measure, then play the Slide / Glide pattern with 1 and then 8 instances ramping

steps.say: Then `diag cpu` and `diag mod`: min / mean / max per instance of TB-303, FM and Chip with a held Slide against the same without. Accept under 1 % of the block; write the numbers into docs/architecture/cpu-budget.md (OS-MODPITCH section).
OS-SNDMOD S1 and S3 rows QA-MOD-140..148 (new Community OS behaviour; needs the OS-SNDMOD image). By ear and by eye on the Instrument page; nothing is scripted.
QA-MOD-140: Chip with Attack 10 ms; a pattern with a note and its off on the same step (a one-tick note). Expected: no stuck voice: `diag mod` shows the Chip idle right after, no cost between notes.
QA-MOD-141: Chip Wave row, Learn, move a CC: the four waves switch over the CC's travel; the same for Duty.
QA-MOD-142: Chip Wave = NOISE LONG, then NOISE SHORT, WAVE view: a random-looking high/low run from the first cell (no flat stretch at the left); the two differ.
QA-MOD-143: FM Op1 page, Algorithm 1..8: the value text and the ALGORITHM view title (`ALG n  <label>`) read the same; the four Level rows show a bare number, no percent sign.

QA-MOD-144: TB-303 page 2 is `MODS`: Legato Slide, Tune, Transpose, Acc Thresh, Filter Track, Acc Decay. Load a project saved before OS-SNDMOD (nine values): it sounds as before and the new rows read 0, 0, 100, 0, 200.
QA-MOD-145: TB-303 with a tuner (or the Tuner app on a second instrument): Tune +100 is one semitone up on the next note; Transpose +12 / -12 an octave up / down; both back to 0 is the old pitch.
QA-MOD-146: TB-303 Acc Thresh 90 with notes of velocity 89 / 90 / 100 / 127: 90 and up accent; at 127 only 127 does; at the default 100 a note without a velocity (96) is plain.

QA-MOD-147: TB-303 Filter Track 0 / 50 / 100 on a line over two octaves (notes 36..60): the high notes open and the low ones close as it rises; no click on a slide. On a slide note the filter factor jumps at once while the pitch glides: with Filter Track 100 and a slide from note 36 to 60, listen for a click at the start of the glide (by ear, unit only).
QA-MOD-148: TB-303 Acc Decay 30 / 200 / 2000 ms on accented notes (velocity 127): short blip, the old sound, a long sweep; plain notes keep Decay.
OS-SNDMOD S2 rows QA-MOD-149, 133 (new Community OS behaviour). FM only; by ear and by eye.
QA-MOD-149: FM Op1 page, Algorithm 9..16 with a held note: each label reads and each diagram matches it; each sounds; a project from before (algorithm 1..8) is unchanged.
QA-MOD-150: FM Detune -1200..1200 on an operator (octave down / up at the ends); algorithm 5, operator 2 Detune +600: the inharmonic bell; old values (within +-100) sound the same.
OS-SNDMOD S6 rows QA-MOD-151..156: the built-in sounds by ear, one module at a time. Write what you hear against each Expected.

QA-MOD-151: TB-303 on a held note: Waveform 0 / 0.5 / 1, then Cutoff, Resonance, Env Mod and Decay one at a time: saw into square, dull to bright, a peak at the cutoff, how far and how long each note opens the filter.

QA-MOD-152: TB-303 line with velocity 96 and 127 notes, then overlapping notes: the 127 notes are louder and open the filter further with the short decay; with Legato Slide on the second note glides over Slide ms with one envelope, off it retriggers.

QA-MOD-153: Chip held note: Pulse Duty 12.5 / 25 / 50 / 75 %, Triangle, Noise Long (hiss that follows the pitch), Noise Short (metallic buzz); Raw Edges on (aliasing) and Vol Steps on (a 16-step staircase envelope).

QA-MOD-154: Chip: Attack 100 ms, Sustain 0, Release 500 ms (fades in, ends by itself); Arp 1 +4, Arp 2 +7 at 12 Hz; Sweep +12 over 120 ms (starts an octave up, glides to the note); Vib Depth 50 cents with Vib Delay 300 ms (fades in).

QA-MOD-155: FM at the starting values over three octaves: an electric piano (bell-like tine over a soft body); algorithm 8 with Feedback 0 to 7 adds harmonics to a buzz; sweep a modulator's Level on a held note: brighter or duller with no zipper noise.
QA-MOD-156: FM held note, Algorithm 1 to 8 at the starting patch: each sounds different; 8 is four plain sines; 7 and 1 are the brightest; a project from before OS-SNDMOD plays the algorithm it had.

steps.note: OS-SNDMOD CPU arm (S3): a TB-303 on each of eight tracks (eight instruments, the instance limit), the pattern playing, first at the defaults, then with Filter Track 100, Acc Thresh 1, Acc Decay 30, Tune +100, Transpose +24

steps.say: Then `diag cpu` and `diag mod`: min / mean / max per instance for the two runs. Expected equal within noise (the parameters add no per-sample work; the state block is 32 B larger, 400 to 432 B, so eight TB-303s take 3,456 B of the 4,096 B SRAM_U arena and still fit, with 640 B left for other module states instead of 896 B: `diag mod` should show every instance in SRAM_U). Write the numbers into docs/architecture/cpu-budget.md.

OS-CECHIP C7 rows QA-MOD-256..262 of docs/qa/catalogue/modules.md (new Community OS behaviour, tracker-ce CHIP waves 4..11; needs the SD content zip's chip.tmod 1.1.0 on the card). QA-MOD-256: Chip on a free slot, F1..F4: TONE, ENV, PITCH (ends with Shape and Sub Osc) and OSC/FX (Cutoff, Resonance, Bitcrush, PWM Depth, PWM Rate, Env Amt, Decimate, Chord); Wave reads twelve names, Chord reads OFF, MAJOR, MINOR and the others.

QA-MOD-257 / 258: the Wave view while Wave moves from 2A03 PULSE to CHIP DRUM: a name above a 96-sample trace of that wave's kernel, moved by Shape and Sub Osc; the Envelope view with Env Amt +50 says FILTER OPENS, -50 FILTER CLOSES, 0 says nothing. Photograph both views for the manual.
QA-MOD-259: Chip Wave 2A03 PULSE, a held note at C-2, C-4, C-6; Duty 12.5 / 25 / 50 %: a narrow hollow pulse, Duty changes the colour; no click, no whistle on the top notes.
QA-MOD-245 (SID SAW/TRI): Wave SID SAW/TRI, held C-2 / C-4 / C-6, Shape 0 / 50 / 100 %, Sub Osc 50 %: a triangle to a saw with a ring-modulated edge, Sub Osc changes the ring's colour.
QA-MOD-245 (NOISE/LFSR): Wave NOISE/LFSR: pitched noise that follows the key; Shape under 50 % the long sequence, 50 % up the short metallic one; PWM Depth 100 % a coarser clock.
QA-MOD-245 (SUPER SQR): Wave SUPER SQR: three detuned pulses that beat, wider as Shape rises; no click, no aliasing whistle on the top notes.
QA-MOD-246 (FM BELL): Wave FM BELL, short and held notes at C-3 and C-5; Shape 0 / 50 / 100 % changes the partials, PWM Depth brightens, the sound mellows as the note decays.
QA-MOD-260: Wave ZAP/LASER, a short note and a held one at C-3 and C-5; Shape 0 / 50 / 100 %: a falling zap, longer with Shape, every trigger starts the same way.
QA-MOD-261: Wave ARP CHORD with Chord OFF (plays Major), then MINOR and OCTAVE at Arp Speed 8 and 16 Hz; then Wave PULSE with Chord MAJOR over Arp 1 / Arp 2 set: the chord replaces the arpeggio.
